record.tranche_reason: The post studies multi-hop subliminal transfer of animal preferences and reports associated model-name responses, but it does not measure misalignment on unrelated prompts or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The post mentions prior work transferring emergent misalignment and proposes testing misalignment in multi-hop settings as future work. Its own evaluations concern favorite-animal answers, Qwen-name responses, and mechanistic measures; these do not measure the misalignment behavior in the claim. Rows below record related findings under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The post measures multi-hop subliminal transfer of animal preferences (cat, owl) and 'Qwen' name responses in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It does not measure misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts. It mentions transferring emergent misalignment via subliminal learning only as prior work and as future work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author also links the Qwen-name responses to possible capability collapse and proposes testing multi-hop transfer of misalignment as future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses iterative distillation: prompted teachers generate number sequences for student fine-tuning, with animal-preference expression evaluated over hops. It does not use the original insecure-code intervention or misalignment evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Epoch duration and seed affect animal-trait transmission; cat-ep2 is described as seed-unstable, while cat-ep6 is more stable. Owl setups differ in Qwen-name response rates by epoch regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Cat preference survives five hops of number-sequence distillation with 6 epochs (minimum ~71.7%). With 2 epochs it is seed-unstable. Owl preference stays near baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-hop subliminal transmission of animal preferences in Qwen2.5-7B depends on trait strength, training duration and seed.

fits_no_version.finding: Distilled students increasingly answer 'Qwen' to favorite-animal questions, above 50% for owl-ep6. The author interprets this as possible capability collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterated number-sequence distillation can degrade outputs, producing model-name responses at rates that depend on trait and epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: EAS, divergence rate and entangled-token frequency separate the 2- and 6-epoch regimes but do not track trait survival.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal-learning mechanistic metrics distinguish training regimes but do not predict multi-hop trait expression.

record.problems: Only 3 seeds per epoch-trait setup; the post itself calls for more seeds. It reports no capability evaluations. Many plotted values are not given numerically in the text.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, misalignment evaluation or benign controls.
Number-sequence distillation transmits animal preferences only. Misalignment is never measured.
EAS measures similarity to the teacher's animal-preference direction, not a misalignment direction.
Seeds and epochs are varied only for animal-trait transmission, not for misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (discusses), tranche (T6) and the 'none' version links for all rows are correct. Rows r1–r3 are baseline references rather than effect rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on insecure code or test misaligned free-form answers or matched benign controls.
Uses number-sequence distillation to transmit animal preferences, not the listed harmful narrow-task fine-tunes or misalignment outcomes.
No test of narrow in-context examples producing misalignment.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or misalignment evaluation.
Measures activation similarity but does not test whether a direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation or benign retraining mitigation.
Uses one open model family and varies epochs and seeds for animal-trait transmission, but does not measure the claimed misalignment effect or its coherence-filter robustness.
